arguments.explanation: Find current Cursor docs on why repos do not appear after signing in on a new machine.

content.text: This account has no Cursor-hosted repos. Checking whether this project is on GitHub so we can tell you how to get it onto the new laptop.

input.description: Show git remotes and branch status

content.text:
Signing into Cursor on the new laptop does **not** copy your old folders over. Cursor only lists repos that this account can reach through GitHub or Cursor’s own repo host — not whatever lived on the previous machine’s disk.

On **this** Cursor account there are currently **no Cursor-hosted repositories**. So if you are looking in Cursor’s repo / codebase list, an empty list is expected unless GitHub is connected.

**If the code is on GitHub**

1. Open [cursor.com/dashboard?tab=integrations](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=integrations).
2. Connect GitHub (or **Manage Connections** if it already shows connected).
3. Install the Cursor GitHub App on the **GitHub user or org that owns the repos**, and grant **All repositories** or the specific ones you need.
4. Fully quit Cursor and reopen it.

Cursor only shows repos that app can access. Org repos need the app installed on that org even if you can see them on github.com. After that, clone the repo onto this laptop (`File > Open Folder` after clone, or clone from the project picker).

**If the code only lived on the old laptop**

It is still only on that machine unless you pushed it somewhere. Copy the project folder over (USB, cloud drive, etc.), or from the old laptop push it to GitHub, then clone it here.

**If you expected Cursor-hosted (Origin) repos**

This login has no Origin namespace, so there is nothing for Cursor to list. Check you used the **same email** as on the old laptop. Origin’s command-line tool is also not supported on native Windows yet; the web list at [cursor.com/codebase](https://cursor.com/codebase) is the place to confirm whether any Origin repos exist.

If you tell me whether you used GitHub, only local folders, or Cursor’s codebase page, I can walk you through the exact next click.

Yes — **put this project on GitHub** if you want it on the new laptop and not only on this machine.

That is the better option for you right now:

- This folder is already a git repo, so GitHub is a natural backup.
- Signing into Cursor does not copy local folders. GitHub does.
- Cursor-hosted repos are not a good fit here: this account has none, and Origin’s CLI is not supported on native Windows.

When you are ready, say the word and I can walk you through creating the GitHub repo and pushing this project (without putting `.env` or other secrets in it). Take your time checking GitHub.
